title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley
description: An ambitious scientist and his creation confront the cost of isolation and responsibility.
rights: Source edition: public domain in the United States. Listed creative contributors screened for India, UK and EU; original licence retained.
editionCredits: Judith Boss, Christy Phillips, Lynn Hanninen and David Meltzer. HTML version by Al Haines. Further corrections by Menno de Leeuw.
longDescription: Atmosphere matters as much as action: unsettling places, uncertainty and emotional intensity shape the experience. Questions of trust, belonging and the limits of human understanding give the story resonance beyond its suspense. Read for the gradually deepening mood without needing to know its surprises in advance.

authorInfo.bio: Mary Shelley was an English novelist who brought Gothic storytelling into conversation with scientific ambition and human responsibility. Frankenstein grew out of a ghost-story challenge in 1816. She also wrote The Last Man, imagining a future transformed by catastrophe.
authorInfo.edition: Source edition and cover supplied by Project Gutenberg. This is the complete text of the supplied edition, including its introductory material.
